long_form.title: The 15-Minute AI Risk Audit for Any Business
long_form.hook: Your team may already be putting confidential data into AI tools. In 15 minutes, you can find the highest-risk gap.
long_form.viewer_intent: A leader wants a fast, non-technical way to inventory AI use and reduce data, authority, and vendor risk.
steps: Inventory every sanctioned and unsanctioned AI use
Classify data before it reaches a model
Map what the tool can decide or change
Verify retention, training, region, and deletion terms
Assign an owner, approval boundary, and review date
long_form.case: A marketing assistant pastes a customer list into a public chatbot; show how the audit catches the data and vendor-control gaps.
long_form.cta: Download the Ai Risk Checklist and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped AI Readiness Assessment.

long_form.title: Passkeys vs Passwords: What Businesses Should Deploy Now
long_form.hook: A stolen password can be replayed. A correctly deployed passkey changes what the attacker has to steal.
long_form.viewer_intent: An IT or business leader is comparing authentication choices and wants a staged rollout plan.
steps: Separate authentication from account recovery
Explain phishing resistance without claiming invincibility
Inventory identity providers and legacy blockers
Pilot administrators and high-risk teams first
Measure enrollment, recovery, lockouts, and bypass paths
long_form.case: Compare a phishing-site lab flow against a passkey flow; show that recovery and session theft remain separate risks.
long_form.cta: Download the Identity Checklist and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Cyber Risk Assessment.

long_form.title: Build an AI Policy Your Team Will Actually Use
title_alternatives: A Practical AI Policy in One Hour
Your AI Policy Is Too Vague
long_form.hook: A policy nobody can apply is not a control. These five decisions turn AI guidance into daily behavior.
long_form.viewer_intent: An owner needs a practical acceptable-use policy with clear data and approval boundaries.
steps: Define allowed, restricted, and prohibited use cases
Classify data and approved tools
Require human review for consequential outputs
Record vendor and output provenance
Create exception, incident, and quarterly review paths
long_form.case: Walk through an employee choosing between an approved summarizer and an unapproved public model for a confidential contract.
long_form.cta: Download the Ai Policy Kit and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped AI Governance Workshop.

long_form.title: Ransomware: Your First 60 Minutes
title_alternatives: What to Do Before Paying Anyone
long_form.hook: The worst first-hour mistake is turning one incident into an organization-wide loss of evidence.
long_form.viewer_intent: A business leader wants a safe, prioritized first-hour response without offensive detail.
steps: Protect life and safety; activate the named incident lead
Isolate affected systems without destroying evidence
Preserve logs, notes, clocks, and decision records
Use out-of-band communications and notify counsel/insurer as applicable
Scope impact before restoration or payment decisions
long_form.case: Use a tabletop clock and fictional ACME workstation alert; distinguish isolation from powering everything off.
long_form.cta: Download the Incident First Hour and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Incident Tabletop Workshop.

long_form.title: AI Agents Need a Permission System, Not Trust
title_alternatives: Never Give an AI Agent These Permissions
long_form.hook: An AI agent does not need bad intent to cause damage. It only needs an overpowered tool and an ambiguous instruction.
long_form.viewer_intent: A technical leader wants architecture controls for tool-using agents.
steps: Give every tool an explicit typed contract
Enforce identity, scope, budget, and time outside the model
Separate propose, approve, execute, and audit states
Make high-impact actions fail closed
Test prompt injection, replay, partial failure, and rollback
long_form.case: A support agent proposes a refund: show read-only analysis, draft, human approval, execution, and append-only audit.
long_form.cta: Download the Agent Control Matrix and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Governed Automation Design.

long_form.title: Crypto Wallet Security: A Business Operations Checklist
long_form.hook: The private key is only one risk. Most business wallet failures happen in the process around it.
long_form.viewer_intent: An operator needs non-investment guidance for custody, approvals, recovery, and audit.
steps: Separate treasury policy from market speculation
Use role separation and transaction approval thresholds
Document key generation, storage, backup, and recovery
Allowlist destinations and verify out of band
Run recovery drills and reconcile an append-only ledger
long_form.case: Use a fully fictional testnet transfer to show proposer/approver separation; never display seed phrases or real balances.
long_form.cta: Download the Wallet Ops Checklist and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Digital Asset Control Review.

long_form.title: Stop Automating Broken Workflows
title_alternatives: The Automation Mistake Costing Your Team
long_form.hook: Automation scales whatever is already there—including ambiguity, errors, and missing approvals.
long_form.viewer_intent: An operations leader wants to choose a safe, high-ROI process to automate.
steps: Write the trigger, inputs, decisions, outputs, and owner
Measure baseline time, error, volume, and exceptions
Remove unnecessary steps before adding tools
Place approvals at consequential decisions
Pilot with rollback, monitoring, and a kill switch
long_form.case: Map a fictional invoice workflow and show why an ambiguous vendor change must remain human-approved.
long_form.cta: Download the Automation Readiness Map and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Automation Discovery Workshop.

long_form.title: Phishing in the AI Era: A Safe Detection Drill
long_form.hook: Perfect grammar no longer tells you a message is safe. Verification has to move outside the message.
long_form.viewer_intent: A viewer wants a safe, current verification routine without enabling attackers.
steps: Pause requests involving money, secrets, or access
Inspect sender context without clicking embedded links
Verify through a known-good channel
Report using the organization process
Preserve the message; never shame the reporter
long_form.case: Use fabricated, clearly labeled emails and a known-good phone directory; do not reproduce a live brand login page.
long_form.cta: Download the Phishing Verification Card and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Security Awareness Workshop.

long_form.title: RAG Security: How Private Data Leaks
title_alternatives: Your AI Search Can Cross Data Boundaries
long_form.hook: Retrieval can make an answer more accurate—and expose a document the user was never allowed to see.
long_form.viewer_intent: An AI builder wants practical authorization, retrieval, and prompt-injection controls.
steps: Authorize before retrieval, not after generation
Preserve tenant and document ACLs in every index
Treat retrieved text as untrusted input
Constrain citations and verify source access
Red-team cross-tenant, indirect injection, and deletion paths
long_form.case: Use two fictional tenants and a poisoned document to show a denied retrieval and a quarantined instruction.
long_form.cta: Download the Rag Threat Model and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Secure AI Architecture Review.

long_form.title: Blockchain Infrastructure Without the Investment Hype
long_form.hook: You can understand blockchain infrastructure without predicting the price of a single token.
long_form.viewer_intent: A business viewer wants a neutral system model rather than trading advice.
steps: Separate networks, assets, applications, and custody
Trace a signed transaction from wallet to propagation
Explain consensus and probabilistic/deterministic finality
Map fees, bridges, oracles, and operational dependencies
Evaluate a use case against a conventional database baseline
long_form.case: Animate a fictional transaction through nodes; label latency and trust assumptions and avoid token price charts.
long_form.cta: Download the Blockchain System Map and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Digital Infrastructure Briefing.

long_form.title: Your SaaS Offboarding Checklist Has a Dangerous Gap
long_form.hook: Disabling email is not offboarding if sessions, API tokens, shared vaults, and automations still work.
long_form.viewer_intent: An IT/operations lead needs a complete and auditable departure process.
steps: Trigger one owned workflow from HR status
Disable identity and revoke active sessions
Rotate shared secrets and transfer owned automations
Recover devices and preserve required records
Verify closure, exceptions, and post-exit monitoring
long_form.case: Show a fictional departed employee whose OAuth token continues running an automation after the mailbox is disabled.
long_form.cta: Download the Offboarding Checklist and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Identity and Access Review.

long_form.title: How to Evaluate an AI Vendor Without Trusting the Demo
long_form.hook: A polished demo tells you almost nothing about retention, failure, access control, or exit cost.
long_form.viewer_intent: A buyer wants a defensible AI procurement and pilot process.
steps: Define the decision and data before viewing the demo
Verify data use, retention, deletion, region, and subprocessors
Test identity, authorization, audit, and admin controls
Measure quality, abstention, latency, and failure on your eval set
Contract for portability, incident notice, and exit
long_form.case: Score a fictional vendor response and visibly mark unknowns instead of converting them into assumed zeros or passes.
long_form.cta: Download the Ai Vendor Scorecard and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped AI Vendor Due Diligence.

long_form.title: Backups Are Not Recovery: Prove You Can Restore
long_form.hook: A green backup dashboard is not evidence that your business can recover.
long_form.viewer_intent: A leader wants to validate recovery time, integrity, and dependencies.
steps: Name the critical service and acceptable RTO/RPO
Choose a clean, isolated restore target
Restore data, identity, secrets, and configuration
Test functional correctness and integrity
Record timing, gaps, owner, and next drill
long_form.case: Restore a harmless sample app in a lab and show how missing encryption keys defeat an otherwise complete data backup.
long_form.cta: Download the Restore Drill and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Resilience Assessment.

long_form.title: Data Lineage: The Missing Layer in AI Trust
title_alternatives: Trace Every AI Answer to Its Source
long_form.hook: If nobody can trace an answer to its source, confidence is decoration—not governance.
long_form.viewer_intent: A data leader needs provenance concepts and an implementable evidence chain.
steps: Assign immutable source and ingestion identifiers
Record transforms, versions, actor, and time
Propagate classification and access policy
Attach citations and confidence to derived claims
Support correction, deletion, replay, and audit
long_form.case: Trace one fictional alert from source event through normalization, entity resolution, model summary, operator correction, and final report.
long_form.cta: Download the Lineage Template and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Data and Ontology Architecture.

long_form.title: Prompt Injection: The Control Models Cannot Provide
title_alternatives: Stop Prompt Injection at the Tool Boundary
Why Better Prompts Won't Secure Your Agent
long_form.hook: You cannot prompt your way out of prompt injection when the model can access powerful tools.
long_form.viewer_intent: An AI engineer wants layered defenses beyond prompt wording.
steps: Mark all retrieved and user content untrusted
Keep secrets and policy out of model-visible context where possible
Allowlist tools, resources, parameters, and egress
Require deterministic authorization and human approval
Evaluate attacks continuously and fail closed
long_form.case: A poisoned fictional web page asks the agent to export records; a policy service denies the unapproved destination.
long_form.cta: Download the Prompt Injection Checklist and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped AI Agent Threat Model.

long_form.title: Build a Governed Automation State Machine in Python
title_alternatives: Code an Automation That Cannot Skip Approval
long_form.hook: This Python state machine makes the unsafe transition impossible—even when an AI recommends it.
long_form.viewer_intent: A developer wants implementable governed automation code.
steps: Model proposed, reviewed, approved, executed, and rejected states
Validate transitions in conventional Python
Bind actor, scope, payload digest, and expiry to approval
Make execution idempotent and append-only audited
Test forbidden transitions and rollback
long_form.case: Live-code a small typed Python example against fake records; unit-test direct proposed-to-executed rejection.
long_form.cta: Download the State Machine Template and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Governed Automation Engineering.

long_form.title: A Practical Cyber Risk Register for Small Business
long_form.hook: A risk register should change a decision—not become a spreadsheet of imaginary precision.
long_form.viewer_intent: A leader needs a lightweight, prioritized risk management method.
steps: Name asset, threat event, vulnerability, and consequence
Use bounded qualitative likelihood and impact
Record existing controls and evidence strength
Assign treatment, owner, due date, and residual risk
Review on change, incident, and a fixed cadence
long_form.case: Score a fictional business-email-compromise risk; distinguish observed evidence from assumptions.
long_form.cta: Download the Risk Register Template and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Cyber Risk Assessment.

long_form.title: Model Routing: Use the Smallest AI That Can Prove the Job
title_alternatives: Stop Sending Every Task to One Model
long_form.hook: The best model for a task is not always the largest. It is the smallest approved route that meets the evidence threshold.
long_form.viewer_intent: An architect wants risk-aware routing across models and deterministic tools.
steps: Classify task, data, latency, and consequence
Prefer deterministic code for hard invariants
Evaluate approved models on a versioned task set
Route with policy, budgets, fallback, and abstention
Log route, version, evidence, cost, and outcome
long_form.case: Route three fictional tasks: arithmetic to code, public summarization to a small model, consequential recommendation to reviewed workflow.
long_form.cta: Download the Model Routing Matrix and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped AI Platform Architecture.

long_form.title: ClearGlassInc Artemis: A Governed Intelligence Architecture
title_alternatives: Inside a Human-Governed AI Intelligence Platform
long_form.hook: Machine-speed analysis does not require machine-made authority. Here is the architecture that keeps the boundary visible.
long_form.search_query: Palantir AIP Foundry Gotham Apollo architecture
long_form.viewer_intent: A technical executive wants a credible target-state system map and governance boundaries.
steps: Separate Gotham operations, Foundry data/ontology, AIP orchestration, and Apollo deployment
Enforce coalition-aware ontology permissions
Capture provenance across event, claim, recommendation, and approval
Run proposal-only self-improvement through eval and review
Deploy versioned artifacts with health gates and rollback
long_form.case: Use a clearly labeled target-state diagram; do not imply Palantir access, partnership, provisioning, or deployed capability.
long_form.cta: Download the Artemis Blueprint and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Artemis Architecture Workshop.

long_form.title: Third-Party Risk: Map the Access You Inherited
title_alternatives: Audit Vendor Access Before the Incident
Your Vendors Are Part of Your Attack Surface
long_form.hook: A vendor can be outside your company and still hold identity, data, code, and recovery power inside it.
long_form.viewer_intent: An owner wants a proportionate vendor inventory and review process.
steps: Inventory services, owner, purpose, and criticality
Map data, privileges, integrations, and support access
Verify identity, logging, incident, backup, and exit controls
Prioritize concentration and irreversibility
Set evidence expiry and remove unused access
long_form.case: Map a fictional payroll provider and reveal an undocumented global admin support path.
long_form.cta: Download the Vendor Access Map and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Third-Party Risk Review.

long_form.title: AI Evals: Stop Shipping on Vibes
long_form.hook: A convincing demo is one example. An evaluation tells you how often the system fails—and where.
long_form.viewer_intent: An AI team wants a practical, versioned pre-deployment eval method.
steps: Define task, rubric, failure cost, and abstention
Create representative and adversarial examples
Score quality, citation, safety, latency, and cost
Compare versions with confidence intervals and human review
Gate promotion, monitor drift, and preserve rollback
long_form.case: Run a small Python evaluation on synthetic support questions; show a candidate that improves fluency but regresses citations and is rejected.
long_form.cta: Download the Eval Harness Template and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped AI Evaluation Sprint.

long_form.title: Can an AI System Improve Itself Safely?
long_form.hook: A safe self-improving system can change a candidate prompt. It cannot change its own authority.
long_form.viewer_intent: A technical leader wants the feedback-to-evaluation architecture with rollback.
steps: Capture corrections and outcomes with consent and lineage
Convert recurring failures into versioned eval cases
Generate candidate prompt, routing, or workflow changes in a sandbox
Require offline gates, security review, and accountable approval
Canary, monitor, rollback, and append the audit record
long_form.case: Follow one operator correction through a fictional candidate, failed security test, revised candidate, approval, canary, and rollback-ready release.
long_form.cta: Download the Improvement Loop Canvas and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Artemis Governance Design.

long_form.title: The Executive Cybersecurity Dashboard That Avoids Vanity Metrics
title_alternatives: Five Cyber Metrics Executives Can Use
long_form.hook: A million blocked events may mean your controls work—or your dashboard has no idea what matters.
long_form.viewer_intent: An executive wants decision-linked security and resilience metrics.
steps: Tie metrics to critical services and loss scenarios
Measure control coverage and evidence freshness
Track detect, contain, recover, and restore outcomes
Expose exceptions, residual risk, and decision owner
Avoid totals without denominator, trend, or consequence
long_form.case: Replace a fictional blocked-events counter with phishing-report time, privileged MFA coverage, restore success, and overdue critical exceptions.
long_form.cta: Download the Cyber Dashboard Template and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped Executive Security Advisory.

long_form.title: Your 90-Day Digital Transparency Roadmap
title_alternatives: From AI Chaos to Auditable Operations
long_form.hook: Transparency is not a dashboard. It is the ability to trace a decision, test a control, and assign an owner.
long_form.viewer_intent: A leader wants a sequenced plan spanning AI, cyber, data, and automation.
steps: Days 1–30: inventory systems, decisions, data, access, and owners
Days 31–60: place controls, evidence, approvals, and recovery tests
Days 61–90: automate measurement and governed workflows
Publish exceptions and residual risk to accountable leaders
Repeat quarterly using evidence, not confidence theater
long_form.case: Combine the prior checklists into one fictional company roadmap with named owners and measurable exit criteria.
long_form.cta: Download the Transparency Roadmap and, if this exposes a material gap, request a scoped ClearGlassInc Transparency Assessment.
